title: Isotope by isotope: which xenon nuclei produce a 248 keV recoil for each interaction, and what isotopically modified xenon could reveal
question: For O1 (elastic; inelastic delta = 300/350/366/380 keV), O4, O6, O10 and L10 at 1 TeV, what fraction of the 225-271 keV and full-ROI rate comes from each xenon isotope, how does the pattern differ between spin-dependent, spin-independent and inelastic interactions, and can 136Xe-depleted, 129Xe-enriched or 136Xe-enriched xenon change the 248 keV rate enough to discriminate L10-like from inelastic interpretations?
headline_result: In 90% 136Xe-enriched xenon the 225-271 keV rate per tonne is 0.106x natural for every spin operator (L10, O4, O6, O10) but 1.00x for inelastic O1 at delta = 366 keV (3.1x at 380 keV), so nine events shared between a natural and an enriched detector (12.8 t yr each at LZ's rate) separate the two interpretations at 3 sigma; 136Xe-depleted xenon changes nothing by more than 10% and 129Xe-enriched xenon needs ~54 events
model_or_mechanism: WimPyDD per-isotope shell-model spectra (diff_rate isotopes_list) for O1 elastic/inelastic, O4, O6, O10, L10 = (q^2/mN^2)O4 - O6 at 1 TeV; composition re-weighting R' = sum R_i (a'_i/a_i)(<A>/<A'>); per-isotope inelastic kinematics; exact binomial two-detector separation
confidence: high for spin/inelastic ratios in 136Xe-enriched xenon (composition arithmetic, nuclear-structure independent for spin operators); medium for SI per-isotope shares (+-10-20%, node positions) and for exposures (assume LZ's rate)
